candidates.title: Developer wants to build 500 modular homes on roof of struggling Sask. mall

candidates.title: Loblaw CEO apologizes to 2 million shoppers for personal data hack, offers free credit monitoring
candidates.description: The CEO of Canada’s largest grocery retailer is apologizing to about two million shoppers for a data breach earlier this year.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Teen accused in girl's vicious attack in Quadeville pleads guilty
candidates.description: The teenager accused of a vicious attack on an eight-year-old girl in the tiny rural eastern Ontario village of Quadeville last year pleaded guilty to one count of aggravated sexual assault on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ontario private school scrutinized over class video surveillance, making kids watch themselves ‘misbehaving’
candidates.description: A former student of a London private school and parents are concerned that children were under constant video surveillance in the classroom and asked to critique the footage with their peers. The matter is being investigated by Ontario’s privacy commissioner.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Workshop in Haines Junction teaches fish canning and connects generations
candidates.description: A fish-canning workshop in Haines Junction, Yukon, helps residents preserve food while also passing knowledge between generations. Participants say the skills can help reduce food waste, save money and keep cultural traditions alive.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Curling Canada CEO sees opportunity to think about future of curling in Canada
candidates.description: Curling Canada chief executive officer Nolan Thiessen wants people thinking big thoughts and asking new questions about the sport.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why Quebec's strategic reserve of maple syrup is running dry
candidates.description: Quebec maple syrup producers say the province's strategic reserve will be "completely depleted" by the end of February. What's going on?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Same scam. 2 countries. Why Canadians don’t get their money back
candidates.description: CBC Marketplace investigates bank scams, a global industry built on fear and deception, and exposes the stark contrast between how victims are treated in the U.K. and Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Police services across Ontario suspend use of Crime Stoppers after CBC investigation
candidates.description: At least eight Ontario police units have now paused their use of the Crime Stoppers program, after CBC News revealed the extent of a massive data leak.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'They destroyed my life': 2 Sask. men imprisoned for exploiting woman from Bangladesh
candidates.description: A Bangladeshi woman who was trafficked and exploited by two men in Saskatchewan — and repeatedly raped by one of them — says she now lives in fear and struggles to trust anyone.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The haunting call of Canada's common loon is becoming less common amid widespread declines, study suggests
candidates.description: A new study published Thursday in the journal FACETS reveals severe declines in loon chick populations across North America over the past three decades or more.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: City councillor calls for independent investigation into fatal Calgary bus explosion
candidates.description: A week after a deadly bus explosion in northeast Calgary, the area councillor is calling for an independent investigation into the crash. But two experts say incidents like this one are rare, and the bus model involved in the crash adheres to strict testing and maintenance guidelines.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada Post starting weekend parcel delivery in Toronto, Montreal and Ottawa this fall
candidates.description: Canada's national mail carrier says it plans to start delivering parcels on the weekend to seven million households by the end of 2027, as part of the financially troubled Crown corporation's major restructuring.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Federal bureaucrats grilled over decision to strip status from over 700 Innu in Quebec
candidates.description: After emotional testimony from members of the Innu First Nation of Essipit in Quebec who’ve seen their lives upended, federal bureaucrats defended their decision to remove status from more than 700 Innu in the community.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge dismisses farmers' class action over end to Canadian Wheat Board monopoly more than a decade ago
candidates.description: A Manitoba judge has dismissed a class-action lawsuit seeking damages for grain farmers following the federal wind-down of the Canadian Wheat Board monopoly, marking what one expert calls the "last chapter" of the wheat board saga.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: First Nations artists pull art from University of Calgary after event inviting debate on residential schools
candidates.description: Two First Nations artists have pulled their work from the University of Calgary’s gallery in a protest over an event that invited students to debate whether residential schools were an act of genocide.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Wolf euthanized after rare attack near Cameco site in northern Sask.
candidates.description: The Ministry of Community Safety says a wolf attacked a person in a remote northern area of the province on Oct. 17.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Top court will hear appeal on ruling that found feds violated Charter during convoy protest
candidates.description: The Supreme Court of Canada will hear an appeal of a 2024 Federal Court ruling that found the government of former prime minister Justin Trudeau infringed the Charter rights of convoy participants when it invoked the Emergencies Act in 2022.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Accused Tumbler Ridge shooting co-conspirator enters not guilty plea in U.S. court
candidates.description: James Cody Bryant entered a not guilty plea in a Seattle courtroom Thursday, for the charge of conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Agent Layla': A sex assault victim went undercover to bring her abuser to justice. Now he's out on parole
candidates.description: A parole board decision to release the man who sexually assaulted her has created a whiplash effect for Vienna Luke, who is simultaneously advocating against Justin Sewell’s release from a halfway house and responding to other women moved by her story
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney says 'direct casualties' are result of Ukraine's restricted access to Musk's Starshield
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney on Friday criticized a decision to restrict Ukraine's access to Elon Musk's military-grade satellite network, saying the move is costing lives.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: A polarized Brazil heads to presidential vote Sunday with economy, corruption top of mind
candidates.description: Frustrations around corruption and feelings of personal financial stagnation driving voting choices as Brazil heads to presidential run-off on Sunday, Oct. 25.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Netanyahu orders West Bank closure as Israeli soldiers, Palestinian gunmen killed in exchanges
candidates.description: The Israeli army says two soldiers were killed in an attack in the occupied West Bank on Friday that also left two Palestinian gunmen dead, prompting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to order the closure of the territory.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Melania Trump, Pope Leo broker humanitarian ceasefire for ravaged Ukraine city Oleshky
candidates.description: Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will ‌begin on Oct. 29, the White House said on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney defends doing business with countries that don’t share Canada’s values
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney defended his government’s pursuit of trade with countries accused of human rights abuses, arguing few nations meet Canada’s standards. Wrapping up a visit to Turkey, Carney insisted engagement does not equal approval, but declined to say whether he personally challenged President Erdogan over his government’s crackdown.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Europe's killer heat this summer claims record 50,000 lives, study suggests
candidates.description: Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hundreds of flights cancelled, schools closed as Typhoon Champi hits Taiwan
candidates.description: Taiwan shut down schools and offices and grounded hundreds of flights as Typhoon Champi brushed by the island Friday, packing strong winds and torrential rains.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Elon, Starlink and the betrayal of Ukraine
candidates.description: SpaceX's Starlink service in Ukraine had its speed throttled recently, causing disruptions to their defense operations during Russian attacks. What does this reveal about big tech's role in modern warfare?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Searches of cellphones, laptops by U.S. customs up more than 32% so far this year
candidates.description: Searches of electronic devices such as phones and laptops of travellers entering the United States are up more than 32 per cent this year and are on track to set a new record, CBC News has learned.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Meta board placates Zuckerberg after threat to leave California if voters approve wealth tax measure
candidates.description: Meta Platforms has struck a deal with Mark Zuckerberg, Reuters has reported, in a move spurred by a California ballot measure, part of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, that has sparked heated debate and hundreds of millions in campaign spending.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tibet earthquake kills at least 16
candidates.description: A magnitude 7 earthquake hit China's Tibet region on Thursday evening, killing at least 16 people, injuring 46 and collapsing hundreds of homes in the northern regional city of Nagqu, official media said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Execution staff warned of possibility some of Christa Pike's veins had 'blown': attorney
candidates.description: Tennessee execution team members failed multiple times to establish working IV lines in Christa Pike's arms before her attempted execution and warned that some of her veins may have ruptured, or "blown," before she was injected with the lethal drug, her attorney wrote in a court document filed Thursday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Gisèle Pelicot and daughter join forces to empower victims of drugging and sexual assault
candidates.description: After a period of estrangement, Caroline Darian says she and her mother, Gisèle Pelicot, are "now, more than ever, together" as they launch a new public awareness campaign about drug-facilitated sexual abuse — also known as chemical submission.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. charges 82-year-old Virginia Democratic lawmaker in alleged drug scheme
candidates.description: U.S. prosecutors accuse L. Louise Lucas of running an illegal cannabis business with members of her family. The 82-year-old Virginia state senator said Thursday's actions amounted to the federal government wielding its "full weight" against a great-grandmother.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 1st human case of livestock virus Shamonda reported in France
candidates.description: France on Thursday reported the first human case of the Shamonda virus usually found in livestock in a patient who later died, with authorities adding there was no risk to the general population at this stage.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New York City council votes to advance bill that would ban horse-drawn carriages
candidates.description: New York City council passed a bill Thursday that would ban horse-drawn carriage rides by June 2028, pulling back the reins after the death of a teenage tourist last spring.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian diplomats based in U.S. advised to avoid appearing with midterm candidates
candidates.description: The government of Canada has issued advice to all embassy and consulate staff to avoid appearing with U.S. midterm candidates, according to a source with knowledge of the notices.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: EU awards human rights prize to International Criminal Court amid Trump attacks
candidates.description: The European Parliament says this year's Sakharov Prize recognizes the International Criminal Court's "important work in upholding international law and justice." The tribunal in The Hague has faced escalating attacks from U.S. President Donald Trump's administration.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Detroit tourism bureau halts advertising in Canada amid trade war, hopes Canadians won't 'hold grudge'
candidates.description: Detroit’s tourism bureau has completely stopped marketing to Canada, saying they understand that the “antagonistic” American actions have strained relations between the two countries.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadians caught up in Trump voter fraud crackdown as U.S. accuses Canada of election interference
candidates.description: Since late last year, federal prosecutors have charged dozens of non-citizens, many of them longtime U.S. permanent residents, with illegally voting in federal elections. At least 15 Canadians have been caught up in the crackdown ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump to exempt some Canadian products from tariffs amid midterm pressure
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump is poised to lift tariffs on some Canadian products as Republicans in border states lobby for relief from trade actions that have put them in a shaky political position ahead of November's midterms.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian planemaker Bombardier investing $270M in U.S. expansion
candidates.description: The company says its looking to hire for 500 roles and plans to add 300 more as it expands in Kansas, Indiana, Texas and Connecticut. U.S. President Donald Trump indicated the expansion was coming in a social media post on Thursday — after he walked back earlier threats to prevent Bombardier from selling in the U.S.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Consumer agency says unclear bank fees can add up for customers
candidates.description: Financial Consumer Agency of Canada says the bigger picture on how much Canadians pay in bank fees might be more murky than it should be, with foreign exchange fees and fees based on usage adding up for less wealthy Canadians in particular.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What is PHP, and how did a flaw in its code lead several websites to go dark this week?
candidates.description: PHP is an open-source computer language that powers an estimated 70 per cent of the internet. While websites being taken offline caused alarm, that was done to implement a fix — which cybersecurity experts say show the system for remedying such issues is working.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Minister gives Stelco owner 15 days to reverse layoffs before turning to the courts
candidates.description: In a demand letter sent to Ohio-based Cleveland-Cliffs, Industry Minister Mélanie Joly says the company is violating its commitments under the Investment Canada Act and it has 15 days to resolve the issue.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Edmonton-based video game studio BioWare shutting down after more than 30 years
candidates.description: Video game publisher Electronic Arts is shutting down the popular Edmonton-based game development studio BioWare, known for the games Baldur's Gate and Dragon Age, after more than three decades.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Airbnb limiting the checkout chores hosts can ask guests to do

candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Deadly shooting near Paris is a 'racist terrorist attack', Macron says
candidates.description: One person is killed and five wounded in a series of attacks and the suspected gunman has been apprehended.

candidates.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say

candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Israeli forces begin demolishing Palestinian buildings in Hebron after two Israeli soldiers shot dead
candidates.description: The soldiers were killed in an attack by two Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint outside the West Bank city on Friday morning.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: White House says Melania Trump brokers truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'
candidates.description: Ukraine and Russia confirm the truce in Russian-occupied Oleshky, where residents have had to eat garden weeds to survive.

candidates.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted

candidates.title: PSG v Lyon moved as Paris prepares for more protests

candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US justice department investigating Corey Lewandowski over DHS role
candidates.description: Trump's former campaign manager is reportedly being investigated for allegedly using his role at the Department of Homeland for financial gain.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit
candidates.description: Trump is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave in 2021.

candidates.title: Newborn twins fight for survival as conflict fuels Yemen's hunger crisis

candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: CCTV footage appears to show gunmen near church in Jordan
candidates.description: Dozens of people had been inside the church for a funeral when the shooting began, local media report.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'It's part of the culture' - New York bans horse-drawn carriages after more than 160 years
candidates.description: The BBC's Madeline Halpert spoke to city tourists, residents and horse carriage workers about the industry and their opinion on the ban.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Damaging hail pelts Phoenix in rare storm
candidates.description: Videos from the Arizona capital show people sheltering inside a car as hail smashes the windscreen, while intense downpours covered neighbourhoods in ice.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Rubio turns to small Indian town as US faces high oil prices
candidates.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio pushed a business and energy agenda over diplomacy on his second trip to India this year.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

candidates.title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI
candidates.description: Indian workers are being paid to film themselves at work and the footage is used to train AI.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax
candidates.description: The Meta boss had said he would exit the state over a wealth tax that has not yet come into force.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning
candidates.description: Governments and companies are scrambling to protect their websites, as Amazon says it experienced attacks before the warning was made public.

candidates.title: Trump's green card curbs test Indian tech workers' American dream

candidates.title: Why is Elon Musk plotting a mega-merger of SpaceX and Tesla?
candidates.description: Musk says there's "a lot to be gained" by combining the firms in what would be the biggest merger in history.

candidates.title: Trains cancelled and roads warnings as Scotland prepares for Storm Boelo
candidates.description: Heavy rain and strong winds are expected during the second named storm to hit in two days, with gusts of up to 80mph forecast.

candidates.description: Millions remain under yellow weather warnings for wind and rain, with a second storm expected to hit Scotland and parts of northern England on Saturday.

candidates.title: October's full Hunter's Moon to light up night sky this weekend
candidates.description: October's full Moon, known as the Hunter's Moon, will rise on Sunday night. Will the weather be in your favour?

candidates.title: Storm Austen hits UK as yellow wind warnings in effect
candidates.description: Disruption to travel is likely as the season's first named storm brings a swathe of powerful winds to south-west England on Friday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.description: The assurance from the National Energy System Operator comes amid concern from its engineers about their ability to ensure adequate supply.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Shock' of first England farmer hit by bird flu this season
candidates.description: The first farmer in England hit by bird flu this season tells of the "emotional roller coaster" of losing 32,000 hens.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Jackdaw decision 'taken outwith Scotland about Scotland's energy'
candidates.description: Scottish Green Mark Ruskell, the SNP’s Keith Brown and Scottish Labour’s Jenny Young weigh up the Jackdaw decision.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Is the UK set to green-light a huge untapped oil field?
candidates.description: Scotland editor James Cook visits Rosebank - the UK's largest known untapped oilfield - in the North Atlantic.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.description: NPR'S Leila Fadel speaks with retired four-star Gen. Joseph Votel about the war in Iran and the U.S. and Israeli objectives for a potential post-election bombing campaign.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Israel orders closure of West Bank after soldiers kill 2 men behind an alleged attack
candidates.description: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched an attack near the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday morning. At least five people were injured, including some critically.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Hacking attempts rise after flaws found in program affecting 70% of websites
candidates.description: Governments around the world are rushing to implement safety measures after AI technology found "severe" vulnerabilities in a key programming language called PHP.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: After nearly 6 years, ex-Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi's son hears her voice
candidates.description: Kim Aris tells NPR his mother sounds strong but is in pain. He says she is held at a residence in the capital.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Brazil's runoff: Lula's legacy vs. Bolsonaro's dynasty
candidates.description: Brazil's tight presidential runoff pits a political giant against a Bolsonaro heir in a battle over the country's political future.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Europe's heat claims 50,000 lives. Climate change blamed for two-thirds of deaths
candidates.description: Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.

candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Greetings from the Brazil-Argentina border, where waterfalls are flowing at near-record rates
candidates.description: The Iguazú Falls span more than a mile across both countries. A rain-soaked October, which scientists link to the Super El Niño, has sent near-record volumes of water surging over the towering cliffs.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why Meta is charging to post more hyperlinks
candidates.description: Social media sites aren't the biggest fans of people leaving via hyperlinks. In fact, Meta has made it subscription-worthy for a Facebook Page to post more than two hyperlinks per month. What's the rationale for companies want to keep you on their site?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Gen Z is 'in the thick' of high housing costs. These candidates aim to solve it
candidates.description: Young candidates who rent or live with parents say their generation is "in the thick" of the country's housing affordability crisis. They argue this gives them new energy to solve it for everyone.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Achy from sitting at a desk all day? Try doing this
candidates.description: Sitting at a desk all day hurts. And it isn't good for us. Strategies to make it a little more comfortable, from eye muscle exercises to alleviate eye strain to a back pain-fighting body movement.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: See how Big Tech is transforming Spain's landscape
candidates.description: A drought-stricken region of northeast Spain has become a focus for American companies searching for locations to place their data centers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How long does it take to save up for a starter home? Twice as long as it did in 2019
candidates.description: A new analysis finds that the average renter household now needs 16 years to save for a down payment and closing costs. Rising rents and other costs have consumed a growing share of household budgets.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Elon Musk says Space X and Tesla are considering a merger
candidates.description: CEO Elon Musk says both Space X and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss the idea of a merger, but a merger would require approval of 50% of shareholders.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Netflix holds quarterly earnings call following leadership shakeup and layoffs
candidates.description: Netflix reported its latest quarterly earnings on Tuesday. It comes as the streaming company has announced a management shakeup and layoffs of more than 1,000 employees.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Will a macaque eat a grape sitting on a pile of poo? A study on germophobia
candidates.description: When an outbreak strikes, humans try to avoid germs. (Remember wiping off groceries at the start of the pandemic?) What about ... monkeys?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why going on a 'say no' retreat is a gift to your future self
candidates.description: It's a day to think about all the upcoming appointments and commitments you're dreading — and then decline some of them. Writer Caroline Sylge shares a suggested schedule for the day.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A GOP congressman voted to cut Medicaid. It covers 62% of his district. Can he win?
candidates.description: Republican U.S. Rep. David Valadao is fighting for reelection in central California. 6 in 10 residents of his district are covered by Medicaid, which he voted to cut last year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: High health costs squeeze workers, even if you have good insurance through a job
candidates.description: About 157 million Americans get their health insurance through work. A survey of employers shows a moderate price uptick this year, but workers still say health costs are a top concern.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Can a dream help you solve a problem? Here's how to try tonight
candidates.description: What can you learn from dreams and how can you remember them and steer them to the topics you wish to dream about. Allison Aubrey and A Martinez discuss the resurgance in dream research and how dreams are a tool for self-discovery.

candidates.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
candidates.description: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With $S^2$, we extend PRH to embodied models and make sensorimotor alignment empirically measurable, offering insight into why an embodied model succeeds beyond its closed-loop success rate.
candidates.author: Yunfei Xie, Howard H. Qian, Shiyi Lan, Kaiyu Hang, Chen Wei

candidates.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
candidates.description: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution. Running all candidate solutions to completion can be computationally demanding, so recent work prunes the candidate pool after generating only a short prefix, committing further computation only to the surviving candidates. Existing pruning strategies divide broadly into two categories: Quality-based methods assign a score to each partial solution and discard those predicted to ultimately lead to an incorrect final solution, while diversity-based methods select partial solutions that follow different reasoning trajectories and are therefore likely to cover different final solutions. The tension between these two objectives is an instance of exploration versus exploitation, yet little to no prior work on pruning exposes this trade-off directly, let alone optimizes it. In this paper, we introduce a pruning procedure that addresses this trade-off directly by optimizing pass@$k$ over the selected solution pool. In particular, it chooses the pool to maximize the probability that at least one of its partial solutions, when continued to completion, yields a correct answer. Because this objective simultaneously rewards high-quality partial solutions and penalizes redundancy among them, quality and diversity are naturally balanced by the criterion itself rather than through separate ad-hoc design choices. On eight open-weight reasoning models, our method outperforms existing quality-based and diversity-based pruning strategies. The gains are particularly pronounced when the pruning procedure keeps a moderate number of partial solutions for continued generation, highlighting the value of directly balancing quality and diversity during pruning.
candidates.author: Mahdi Salmani, Adel Javanmard, Devansh Gupta, Meisam Razaviyayn

candidates.title: OpenTac: An Open Ecosystem for Customizable, Scalable, and Transferable 3D Tactile Sensing
candidates.description: We present OpenTac, a novel sensor and a full-stack ecosystem for tactile skins that are highly customizable, scalable, and readily deployed in downstream robot control and learning applications. Our core contribution is twofold. First, we develop a scalable resistive tactile skin with a structured deformable overlay that converts tangential loading into spatially varying pressure. Differential responses across neighboring "taxels" support decoding of local shear vectors, and the common-mode response encodes normal force. Second, we provide a highly customizable sensor design tool that is able to automatically generate fabrication files for these tactile skins from 2D outlines and developable 3D surfaces, including from abstract descriptions such as text (e.g., "design a sensor for a size 9 shoe insole"). We develop an ecosystem around the OpenTac sensor, including the CAD design tool, a sensor simulator, cross-sensor transfer, and fast/adaptive data acquisition. We demonstrate the broad applicability of the OpenTac-CAD sensor design tool by designing and fabricating more than 30 sensors across a variety of robot embodiments. We characterize the three-dimensional tactile fields produced by OpenTac with a commercial, high-precision force/torque sensor. We demonstrate the broad applicability of 3D tactile sensing across contact-rich feedback control and manipulation policy learning on four real-world robot embodiments. Additionally, adaptive acquisition enables kilohertz-rate partial readouts, exceeding full-array raster scanning on the same sensor by 19.2X at 16 sampled taxels per update for a 1024-taxel skin. We provide all hardware, software, and result videos are at opentac.github.io
candidates.author: Ariel Slepyan, Geeta Chandra Raju Bethala, Jiafeng Gu, Anagha Rajendra Dangle, Yinzhe Zhou, Hongyuan Fu, Jade Sim, Tuhin Basu, Xinyi Yin, Md Faizal Karim, Gregory Hager, Homanga Bharadhwaj, Anand Bhattad, Krishna Murthy Jatavallabhula, Nitish V. Thakor

candidates.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
candidates.description: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage. We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting. Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis. The strongest prompted configuration reaches 0.477 accuracy on a stratified 1,000-ticket test subset, versus 0.879 for fine-tuned DistilBERT on the same tickets. Isotonic lowers expected calibration error without reliably improving discrimination: GPT-4o-mini few-shot has one confidence value before and after recalibration and correctness AUROC 0.500. We therefore report correctness AUROC and tie-aware risk-coverage area alongside ECE. At the analytically derived break-even probability 0.80, seven prompted configurations defer all tickets; Haiku few-shot routes only 19/1,000. An LLM-only agreement control and margin/entropy rejection baselines further separate calibration from discrimination. The findings are scoped to this dataset, prompt design, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; the work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or universal deployment certification.
candidates.author: Sachin Gupta

candidates.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
candidates.description: Meta-reinforcement learning aims to train agents that adapt quickly to unseen tasks from limited interaction, but this requires representing task evidence over long interaction histories. Classical recurrent agents compress experience into hidden states, while transformer-based agents retrieve from past trajectories at quadratic memory and computation cost. In this work, we propose Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation (METTA) for meta-reinforcement learning. It decomposes the fast adaptation phase into two temporal scales: a causal neural memory performs fine-grained within-episode adaptation with linear sequence complexity, while compact episode-level summaries support long-range cross-episode task inference without attending over the full interaction history. Moreover, equipping agents with neural memory provides sufficient expressive capacity and test-time training capability, enabling effective adaptation to unseen held-out tasks and task families at meta-test time. On unseen held-out Meta-World ML10/45 test environments, METTA achieves a success rate over $50\%$ while maintaining a low training budget and short wall-clock time. On long-context sparse-reward PointMaze tasks, it outperforms transformer-based baselines by exhibiting more structured exploration behavior. These results show that METTA provides an efficient path toward more adaptive and scalable long-context meta-RL.
candidates.author: Ali Najar, Hosein Hasani, Amir Kooshan Fattah, Yasamin Rajabi, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah

candidates.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
candidates.description: Tool-using language model agents rely on environmental facts to decide whether an action is permitted. When a tool response omits a safety-relevant fact, an agent may carry out a prohibited action even though the user request is benign and every returned statement is true. We introduce \bench{}, an executable benchmark for evaluating unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery in LLM agents under missing evidence. It contains 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains. By systematically suppressing critical facts, the benchmark measures unsafe execution under critical evidence omission and determines the minimum observed failure cardinality, including failures with full evidence and cases with no observed failure after exhaustive testing. An independent audit tool tests whether agents seek missing facts and then withhold prohibited actions while completing permissible tasks. The benchmark reveals substantial variation across the ten models in omission robustness, evidence acquisition, and appropriate action. Resistance to missing evidence does not necessarily translate into useful recovery. Recovery access reduces unsafe execution for all ten models, but agents differ in whether they actively obtain the missing facts and use them to act appropriately in both worlds.
candidates.author: Qijin Zhang, Hanzhen Wang, Yuehan Zhao, Haoyu Dai, Yao Shu, Zhongxiang Dai, Shuang Qiu

candidates.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
candidates.description: Many recent open-weight language models use n-gram embedding tables to improve performance. These tables store learned representations of short token sequences, such as pairs or triples of consecutive tokens, which the model retrieves during processing. However, they can require substantial memory: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, for example, allocates 196 billion parameters to its Engram n-gram memory. We therefore investigate whether this memory cost can be reduced while preserving the performance improvement that the tables provide. We propose storing n-gram embeddings at low precision and systematically investigate different quantization methods and bit allocations across tables. Across nanochat-, Llama-, and GPT-2-family models trained from scratch, four-bit tables save approximately 75% of table memory while preserving more than 99% of the validation-loss improvement from adding the tables. Using fewer bits leads to a larger drop in performance, although we find that a short fine-tuning phase recovers a significant part of this loss. In addition, reinvesting the saved memory in larger tables can improve performance beyond that of the original full-precision tables while still using less memory. These table memory savings also extend to large existing models: on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, low-bit tables save 47-55% of table memory, with perplexity increases of less than 1.2% and largely preserved downstream task performance. These findings establish low-bit precision as a practical way to reduce the memory requirements of n-gram embeddings and use the saved capacity to improve model performance.
candidates.author: Stephen Chung, Wenyu Du

candidates.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
candidates.description: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits step-by-step rationales that appear to explain model predictions, but there is no guarantee these steps causally drive the final answer. In standard autoregressive generation, dense attention allows each reasoning step to attend to the full context, enabling the model to derive answers through direct lookup while generating plausible-sounding but post-hoc justifications. We introduce CausalCoT, an inference framework that enforces causal transparency by decomposing problems into a directed acyclic graph of atomic sub-questions, evaluating each node in an isolated context containing only its direct causal parents. This Markovian structure removes attention pathways to non-parent content, making downstream predictions sensitive to local reasoning rather than global context leakage. Across a diverse suite of reasoning benchmarks, CausalCoT preserves competitive predictive performance while improving explanation faithfulness, increasing causal sensitivity of intermediate reasoning steps by an average of 12 and up to 21 percentage points over the strongest baseline. The structured dependency graph additionally enables test-time interventions in which local corrections propagate predictably through downstream reasoning.
candidates.author: Gabriele Dominici, Teague McMillan, Fazl Barez, Marc Langheinrich, Martin Gjoreski

candidates.title: Can an Agent Debug a Web Corpus? Agentic Auditing of Slovak FineWeb2
candidates.description: Multilingual pipelines such as FineWeb2 apply one recipe across a thousand languages, leaving the failure modes of individual languages unanticipated. We use an LLM once, as a corpus debugger rather than a classifier: a tool-using agent explores the corpus through a read-only, budgeted API and compiles each finding into an executable test, which a native speaker then validates. On the 26.5M-document Slovak portion of FineWeb2, three runs costing \$2.21-\$2.84 each found seven findings over four phenomena. The largest is a machine-generated content farm of 1,408,437 documents (5.32%) that passed the pipeline's filters, 86.6% of it passing even stricter thresholds. Blinded labels support 6 of the 7 findings (defect rates .53-1.00 against .08 in a random control) and do not support one. The compiled suite scans the full corpus in 0.7 s of wall-clock time without a GPU, against \$12k-\$90k per LLM classification pass. The best static sampling baseline validates more selectors than any agent run, at under half the cost. The agent contributes exact prevalence, a precision estimate checked against sampled documents, an account of why the pipeline missed each slice, and a reusable test. We release the framework, Slovak test suite, validation data and agent trajectories.
candidates.author: Marek Šuppa, Ivan Vykopal, Jaroslav Kopčan

candidates.title: Extending Harmonic Function Methods via Root Locus for Coordinated Path Generation
candidates.description: We consider the offline generation of coordinated paths for N interchangeable robots and N goals in planar environments with polygonal obstacles. After a conformal map to a circular domain, starts and goals become the poles and zeros of a rational function R, and the paths are the branches of its Generalized Root Locus (GRL), i.e. the streamlines of the logarithmic potential -log R. We show that, for every phase outside a finite set of critical phases and a set of boundary phases, the induced gradient motion drives each robot to a distinct goal along pairwise disjoint paths that never reach the obstacles; the robot-goal assignment is produced by the construction, and with the gain used as a clock all robots move as the closed-loop roots of the GRL and arrive together at a prescribed time. Obstacles become streamlines through successive Milne-Thomson reflections, and for a finite number of reflections a finite test certifies safety for the potential that is actually computed. Reciprocal root-locus planning is recovered as a special case. The method is illustrated on two polygonal workspaces, 100 random instances compared with independent harmonic planning and artificial potentials, and a scene with ten robots and ten obstacles.
candidates.author: Matteo Frascarelli, Lucia Pallottino, Alberto Landi

candidates.title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
candidates.description: Instrumental convergence is often invoked as a general reason to expect capable agents to acquire or express power-seeking subgoals: self-preservation, resource acquisition, deception, or resistance to oversight which poses an important threat to the society. For LLMs, reinforcement learning is the first stage of post-training that directly optimizes behavior against an objective; therefore, it is the stage where convergent instrumental behavior, on IC grounds, likely to appear. Does reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) make a model more likely to express instrumental-convergence behavior, or does this depend on the training regime, evaluation frame, and stage of post-training? We study this question as a checkpoint-conditioned behavioral trajectory rather than as a single before/after safety score. Using InstrumentalEval, we evaluate OLMo-3-7B-Think across SFT, DPO, 13 intermediate RLVR checkpoints, and the final RLVR model. The trajectory is nonmonotonic: instrumental rate rises from 25.0% at SFT to 46.1% near RLVR step 200, then falls to 11.8% at the final checkpoint. Paired item-level tests and step-wise regression support the final SFT-to-RLVR reduction. Prompt framing does not explain this pattern: a harmful-prompt indicator combined with other framing effects explains only 15% of within-checkpoint score variance on average, and Iterative Null-space Projection (INLP) removes a detectable framing direction without changing the SFT-to-final-RLVR gap. Together with preliminary 32B endpoint results (35.53% SFT to 22.37% RLVR final), these findings indicate that RLVR does not monotonically increase instrumental behavior in this setting: the rate rises early, then falls below the SFT baseline. The result is specific to this model family and benchmark, and judge agreement is moderate, so absolute rates should be read cautiously.
candidates.author: Barış Alparslan, Sandy Tanwisuth, Caleb Petterson

candidates.title: Bilingual Language Models Capture Cross-Linguistic Influence in Second-Language Reading
candidates.description: While monolingual language model (LM) surprisal is widely established as a predictor of reading times, it cannot capture the non-native (L2) reading dynamics that are shaped by the reader's first language (L1). In this work, we investigate whether the cross-lingual transfer within bilingual models aligns with human L1-driven biases during L2 reading. We evaluate bilingual models on eye-tracking data of readers from 12 diverse L1 backgrounds reading English texts. To isolate L1-specific transfer, we compare bilingual models trained on an L1 that matches the readers' L1 background to both a monolingual English baseline and bilingual models trained on other L1s. We demonstrate that matching the readers' L1 improves the prediction of L2 reading times. This predictive advantage is concentrated in late-stage eye-tracking measures, modulated by L1-L2 script overlap, and peaks among intermediate-proficiency readers. These findings provide evidence that bilingual LMs capture aspects of cross-linguistic influence, and that such influence is present in L2 reading behavior.
candidates.author: Abderrahmane Issam, Irene E. Winther, Stefan L. Frank
